title: CWRU vs UM: tuition, size, location
summary: Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) versus University of Miami (UM). Also searched as UM vs CWRU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Case Western Reserve University vs University of Miami (CWRU vs UM) differ in several key aspects. Both institutions are private nonprofit universities, as indicated by College Scorecard ownership code 2. CWRU, located in Cleveland, has an undergraduate enrollment of 6,437 students, whereas UM in Coral Gables enrolls 12,913 undergraduates. Tuition costs also vary, with CWRU charging $66,608 for in-state tuition compared to UM's $62,616. These distinctions highlight differences in size, location, and cost between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Cost is a significant factor when comparing Case Western Reserve University vs University of Miami (CWRU vs UM). Both universities charge the same tuition for in-state and out-of-state students, with CWRU's tuition set at $66,608 and UM's at $62,616. Despite the similarity in tuition fees, the median debt for students who complete their degrees differs between the two institutions. Graduates from CWRU carry a median debt of $24,000, while those from UM have a lower median debt of $17,500. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments students may face at each university.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Case Western Reserve University vs University of Miami (CWRU vs UM) offer distinct learning environments shaped by their campus locations and student populations. CWRU is situated in Cleveland, Ohio, providing an urban setting with an undergraduate enrollment of 6,437 students. In contrast, UM is located in Coral Gables, Florida, and has a larger undergraduate body of 12,913 students. These differences in campus size and geographic context contribute to varied academic and social experiences for students at each institution.

sections.heading: Accreditation
paragraphs: Case Western Reserve University vs University of Miami (CWRU vs UM) both hold accreditation from recognized regional accrediting bodies, ensuring that they meet established standards of quality in higher education.
